The testing promise

Try the check I run on every site

Before any site reaches you, it gets opened at real device sizes and worked through, link by link. Switch sizes below and watch the layout adapt — then run the check.

  • Layout fits the screenNothing overflows, nothing needs sideways scrolling — at this exact width.
  • Every link & button tappedNavigation, calls to action, and contact buttons — each one actually pressed.
  • Text stays readableType scales down gracefully instead of shrinking into a blur.
  • Dark mode checked tooIf your phone is in dark mode, the site has to look right there as well.

This is the same pass your site gets before delivery — you receive the finished version, not a first draft.

Process

How a project runs

Simple, in the open, and built around testing — the same way I build games: one piece at a time, each piece checked before the next.

01

Tell me the goal

A short chat about what the site or clips need to do — more calls, more bookings, more followers. No jargon, no pressure.

02

I build a first version

You get a real working draft fast — actual pages and content, not a picture of a website.

03

I test it hard

Phone and desktop, every link clicked, dark mode checked. Broken things get fixed before you ever see them.

04

You review the finished thing

Your turn — on a version that already works. We polish wording, photos, and details together.

Questions

Before you ask

How much does a website cost?

It depends on scope — a one-page Starter Site is the cheapest way in, a Full Site costs more because there's more to build and test. Tell me what you need in the brief below and I'll give you one straight quote before any work starts. No hourly meter running, no surprise add-ons.

How long does a site take?

A Starter Site is a days-not-weeks job once I have your wording and photos. Bigger sites take longer, and I'll give you a realistic date in the quote — then build and test in stages so you see progress, not silence.

Do I need to test the website myself?

No — that's my job. I open every page at phone, tablet, and desktop sizes, click every link and button, and check dark mode before you get the link. You review the finished version and tell me what to polish.

How does clipping work — what do I send you?

Just a link. Paste the VOD or video link when we talk, and I pull the best moments, caption them, frame them vertical, and send back clips ready to post — each with a caption that credits the original streamer and links the source.

Is reposting clips a copyright risk?

It can be, and I'll be straight about it: crediting the streamer is the right habit, but credit alone isn't permission. The safest clips are your own streams, streamers who welcome clips, or clips with your own commentary added. I'll help you stay on the right side of that line.
